name: Two-Extension Lifts Refute Direct Corner Descent
statement: Let $X$ be a two-extension lift satisfying the exact two-corner conclusion of the lift theorem. Then neither corner $c$ has $X\setminus\{c\}\in\operatorname{Obs}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{amp}})$. Consequently, direct corner descent can fail even at an ample forbidden pc-minor having exactly two corners.
proof: Deleting the upper exclusive corner produces $(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$. The exact peripheral-expansion test shows that this family is not corner-peelable because its duplicated site $S$ is not corner-peelable. Its upper-semicube restriction is the proper pc-minor $S$, also outside the dismantlable-ample class, so the deletion is not pc-minimal and cannot be a forbidden pc-minor. Reversing the two layers gives the same conclusion after deleting the lower exclusive corner.
comments: This is a failure of descent between minimal obstructions: both corner deletions remain nonpeelable but already contain the seed obstruction as a proper pc-minor.
